name: Emerald Signature
why: Same emerald and beige you already know, so nothing feels foreign. Tighter spacing, a clearer type ladder, the new month-to-US$100K bar under the hero, and softer card edges. Lowest risk, fastest to ship.

name: Stone Daylight
why: Stone background with emerald cards and near-black headlines, straight from the print brand kit. Easiest to read outdoors and in daylight, and it looks like your decks and PDFs. Good if HQ is mostly a daytime phone habit.

name: Midnight Glass
tag: Near black, frosted cards, beige glow
why: The luxury app feel: almost black base, translucent frosted cards, soft beige light behind the hero. Numbers pop, the globe looks like it is floating. Best if you want HQ to feel like a private members app.

name: Bento Board
why: The whole day in one screen of tiles, no scrolling for the essentials: next action, money ring, US$ month, waiting counts, views, top post. The layout Apple and Linear use for a reason. Best for a quick glance between filming.

name: Editorial
why: Wide-spaced Montserrat Light caps, hairline rules instead of cards, huge numerals. It reads like a luxury travel magazine and matches your brand headings exactly. Best if you want HQ to look like nobody else’s dashboard.

name: Command Center
why: Built like a trading desk: a stat strip across the top, status lights on every row, tabular numbers, and the US$100K tracker as the headline. Most information per screen of the ten. Best if you want to run the business from one glance.

name: Golden Hour
why: Opens on a full-bleed golden-hour photo that fades into emerald, the same look as your stories and brand world. The dashboard sits under it like an app over a wallpaper. Best if you want HQ to feel like the lifestyle, not a spreadsheet.

name: Focus Mode
tag: One thing on screen at a time
why: Deliberately empty. One giant next action fills the screen with a single button, and everything else sits in a thin strip you expand when you want it. The ADHD-friendly design: no noise until the money task is done.

name: Card Deck
tag: Approve as a stacked swipe deck
why: Approve becomes a single stacked deck in the middle of the screen with two big round buttons, Skip and Send, like the apps people cannot put down. Home gets a story strip of your tabs up top. Best for clearing 20 DMs in two minutes with one thumb.

name: Soft Sage
tag: Calm, rounded, white cards on sage
why: Pale sage background, white rounded cards, emerald buttons and gentle shadows. Feels like a calm wellness app instead of a control room, which is a nice reset on a stressful day. The friendliest of the ten, and still fully on brand.
